+---
+assignees:

+title: Make the integration job on each push take 10 minutes or less
+---
+## Problem
+
+The CI job "Integration (opt-in, real dependencies)" takes approximately 41 minutes on each push to main. The user wants 10 minutes or less.
+
+Evidence: run 36951032341 (commit ef905bf, 2026-10-02). The builds take approximately 5 minutes ("Build the nested integration package" 1m52s, "Build the root products the integration suite starts" 3m01s). "Run the selected integration tests" takes 2136 s for 60 tests. The run of 2026-09-29 (36609306669) took 2080 s.
+
+## Where the time goes
+
+| Group | Tests | Time |
+|---|---|---|
+| Scenarios graded on their answer, on `Qwen3.8-27B-mxfp4` (`multitool-cli-demo` profile) | 13 | approximately 1290 s |
+| Discovery grading (`gradeDiscoveryRounds`, `NoDescriptionSurfaceDiscoveryTests`) | 5 | approximately 780 s |
+| Plumbing and other tests | 42 | approximately 70 s |
+
+Causes:
+
+1. `ci.yml` sets `integration-no-parallel: true`. All scenarios wait for one model at `LiveProfileTurnstile`, so the step time is the sum of the test times. This rule stays.
+2. `discoveryRoundCount = 3` (`IntegrationTests/.../Support/DiscoveryGrading.swift:14`). In both runs, rounds 1, 2 and 3 of each group give exactly the same results (for example `agentSurfaceDiscovery` correctTotal=18 wrongTotal=1 in all 3 rounds). Rounds 2 and 3 cost approximately 500 s and give no information.
+3. Each test resolves its profile again and loads its models again: approximately 9 s for each of 20 resolutions. Example: the weather scenario did `resolve` at 21:28:44 and its first submission at 21:28:53.
+4. One 27B turn takes approximately 15 to 26 s, and a scenario has 3 turns or more. Example: the weather scenario took 66.6 s: approximately 9 s of load, 26 s for the first turn, 17 s for selection and the second turn, and 14 s for the tool call and the answer.
+
+## Work
+
+1. On each push and pull request, run only the build, the plumbing tests and the discovery tests.
+2. Run the 13 answer-graded scenarios on the 27B model in a separate workflow, nightly (on a schedule) and on `workflow_dispatch`. Do not change these suites to a smaller model: the repo rule says that a suite that grades an answer uses `CLIRunner.demoProfile`, the model that a host gets.
+3. Set `discoveryRoundCount` to 1, and change its doc comment to give the measured reason: the rounds gave the same results. If the selection is not deterministic, show it with evidence before you keep more than 1 round.
+4. Resolve each profile one time for each test process, and use it again in the next test, if Router permits it. If Router does not permit it, record the reason on this card.
+5. If it is necessary for the budget, cache the build directories between runs.
+
+Make the split with the inputs of the shared workflow `swissarmyhammer/workflows/.github/workflows/swift-ci.yaml` (`integration-*`, `SWIFT_TEST_FILTER`). If the shared workflow has no input for this split, record what input is necessary; do not change the shared workflow from this repo. Update `CIWorkflowTests`, which pins the `ci.yml` call and its inputs.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- [ ] The integration job of a push to main takes 10 minutes or less, from start to end, in a real CI run. Record the run id.
+- [ ] The 27B answer-graded scenarios run in a scheduled workflow that can also be started by hand, and that workflow ran once with its run id recorded.
+- [ ] `discoveryRoundCount` is 1, and its doc comment gives the measured reason.
+- [ ] `CIWorkflowTests` passes.
+- [ ] `swift test` passes, and `swift build --build-tests --package-path IntegrationTests` passes.
+#ci
\ No newline at end of file
